steps.shell:
python3 - <<PY
from PIL import Image,ImageDraw
a=Image.open('$OUT/41-window-640x360.png')
b=Image.open('$OUT/40-window-1280x720.png')
c=Image.open('$OUT/42-window-1920x1080.png')
sz=a.size
# crop the same relative centre region from each and normalise (nearest) to 400x200
out=Image.new('RGB',(1280,290),(24,24,28))
for im,x,label in ((a,0,'640x360'),(b,440,'1280x720'),(c,880,'1920x1080 requested')):
    w,h=im.size
    reg=im.crop((int(w*0.375),int(h*0.389),int(w*0.625),int(h*0.611))).resize((400,200),Image.NEAREST)
    out.paste(reg,(x,60))
d=ImageDraw.Draw(out)
d.text((10,20),'640x360',fill=(240,240,240))
d.text((450,20),'1280x720',fill=(240,240,240))
d.text((890,20),'1920x1080 requested (window stays 1280x720 in this harness)',fill=(240,240,240))
d.text((10,272),'Stretch is disabled: the pixel grid is derived from the window size.',fill=(200,200,200))
out.save('$OUT/43-pixel-scale-compare.png')
PY

items.check: The same Knight view at 640x360 and 1280x720; pixels get finer as the window grows, framing unchanged. The 1920x1080 request is documented with the harness cap.
items.notes: This harness cannot resize the game window above 1280x720: --window-match resize reports 1920x1080 but the X window and the pixel viewport stay 1280x720 (no black margins, just no growth). Per the brief the item records the supported size: 40 is 1280x720, 41 is 640x360, 42 is the actual 1280x720 frame and is labelled as the requested 1920x1080 that the harness could not deliver, and 43 is a two-size compare with that note instead of faking a third panel. 44 resizes 1280 -> 960 -> 1280 live.
